idea: YouTube channel explaining company analysis visually
buyer: Sponsors and, eventually, a course or subscription audience
pain: Financial explanation is visually terrible and her design eye is wasted
price: Ad and sponsor revenue, later a product
verdict: A genuine visual advantage in a field with none, but the payback horizon is years not months.

why.distribution: Zero audience, and YouTube growth for finance explainers is slow and competitive.
why.demand: Inferred; viewers do not pay directly and sponsors need scale.
why.fmf: An architect's visual training applied to financial explanation is a real and visible differentiator.
why.revenue_structure: Ad and sponsorship income, volatile and platform-dependent.
why.defensibility: Visual craft at this standard is genuinely hard for competitors to match.
why.leverage: Full media leverage with an asset that keeps earning.
why.tailwind: Retail investing interest is real; the platform is saturated.
why.ceiling: Sub-£20k in year one; meaningful revenue is a year-three question.

ceiling_arithmetic: Finance YouTube monetises at roughly £5-15 per thousand views. Even 500,000 views in year one is £2.5-7.5k. Meaningful income requires an audience built over years. Structurally near zero in year one.
carries: A rare and visible aesthetic advantage in a category where everyone else uses ugly slides. It compounds.
kills: Year-one revenue is effectively zero and the audience-building horizon is measured in years.
test: Publish six videos and measure whether view counts grow without her sharing them.
test_pass: Organic growth curve after episode four.
test_fail: Views track exactly with her own sharing.
